=== P1 #1: record() crashes on an undefined error payload and masks the original error ===
FILE: pipeline/src/services/feed/feedq-retrieve-client.ts (run() finally at ~line 245) and pipeline/src/services/feed/trace.ts (record() at ~line 121).
THE BUG: in run(), every error branch (feedq-not-found, exit 2, exit != 0, non-JSON stdout) leaves `tracePayload` undefined, then the finally calls `options.trace.record(call, tracePayload)`. The real `FeedTraceRecorder.record` (trace.ts line 124) does `writeJsonAtomic(join(runDir, relPath), fullPayload)` with fullPayload=undefined; writeJsonAtomic does `JSON.stringify(undefined)` which returns the value `undefined`, and `writeFileSync(tmp, undefined)` throws a TypeError. Because this happens in the finally, the TypeError REPLACES the original FeedqQueryError/FeedqUsageError the caller should see. The existing "records on error" unit tests pass only because they inject a FAKE recorder that never calls writeJsonAtomic, so the crash is invisible (hollow test).
FIX (both layers, defense in depth):
  1. trace.ts record(): coerce an undefined fullPayload to null before writeJsonAtomic, so record() can never crash regardless of caller. A traced error call must still get a payload file (write `null`, or a defined value) and a valid payload_path.
  2. feedq-retrieve-client.ts: on the error branches, set tracePayload to a DEFINED diagnostic object (mirror how feedq-adapter.ts records its error payload, e.g. { status, stderr } / { message }), so the error call's payload file carries something useful rather than bare null. The original FeedqQueryError/FeedqUsageError must still propagate to the caller unchanged.
  3. DE-HOLLOW the test: the "records a failed retrieve/deref call" tests in pipeline/test/feedq-retrieve-client.test.ts must exercise the REAL createFeedTraceRecorder against a temp run dir (or otherwise actually invoke writeJsonAtomic), so the test would FAIL if record() crashed on the error path. Assert that the original FeedqQueryError/FeedqUsageError still throws AND that the error call was recorded with error set and a readable payload file. Prove non-tautological (break the coercion, watch it fail, revert).

=== P1 #2: feed-trace.json index is lost on any pre-flush throw, and resume-append breaks ===
FILE: pipeline/src/agents/pipeline/index.ts. `feedTraceRecorder.flush()` is called exactly once at ~line 2624, AFTER the step loop. Payload files (feed-calls/<seq>.json) and step-trace-<step>.json are written incrementally, but the call INDEX feed-trace.json lands only via that one flush. The body-wide finally at ~line 2764 ends the maintenance span and calls otel.flush(), but NEVER flushes the feed trace recorder. So any throw before 2624 (e.g. an ingest failure, which records its call then re-throws) leaves orphan payload files + step-trace but no feed-trace.json. This contradicts trace.ts's own doc comment and the plan section 2.3 promise ("a crash mid-run leaves valid traces up to the failure point") and defeats the failure-analysis purpose (D2B-6). It also breaks resume: a failed run never flushed, so a resumed run's createFeedTraceRecorder finds no index, restarts seq at 1, and OVERWRITES the prior orphan feed-calls/001.json.
FIX: guarantee feed-trace.json is flushed on EVERY exit path. Add a `feedTraceRecorder.flush()` in the body-wide finally (~line 2764), wrapped in its own try/catch so a flush failure can never mask the real run error. flush() writes the whole in-memory calls array and is idempotent, so keep the existing success-path flush at ~2624 (or rely solely on the finally, your call, as long as the success path still flushes before persistArtifacts rebuilds the manifest, since persistArtifacts calls addFeedCallFilesToManifest). Confirm ordering: the manifest that persistArtifacts builds must still include feed-trace.json and the payload files on a successful run.
TEST: add/extend a test proving (a) a FAILED ingest run still writes feed-trace.json containing the failed call (error set), reconciling with the payload file on disk; and (b) a recorder created over an existing (failed-run) trace continues seq numbering from the prior max and does NOT overwrite feed-calls/001.json. Non-tautological.

CONSTRAINTS: minimal, correct, no legacy, no dead code, no scope creep beyond these two P1s and their tests. Do not touch consumer-step code. Keep the trace.ts doc comment honest with the new behavior. Match repo style.
